title: Compute a profit target for open positions regardless of today's signal
description: suggest_profit_target is currently BUY-only (only computed for a fresh BUY signal, per backend-profit-target's own decision). Ch. 53, read directly, doesn't gate profit targets to entry day only -- a target set at entry is meant to be tracked for the life of the trade, not recomputed only while the signal happens to say BUY. An already-held position whose signal has since drifted to HOLD/SELL currently has no displayed target at all. Depends on backend-profit-target-weekly-channel landing first so this builds on the corrected (weekly-based) target computation, not the one being replaced.

checklist.step: Decide whether an open position's displayed profit target should be computed off the position's actual entry (regardless of today's signal) instead of requiring a fresh BUY signal, and record the rationale -- this revisits backend-profit-target's own prior BUY-only decision explicitly, engaging with why it was made and why ch.53's primary source now changes the analysis.
Implement the decided behavior in GET /api/portfolio/risk (or wherever an open position's target is surfaced).
Update/add tests covering a held position whose signal has drifted to HOLD/SELL, confirming a target is still shown per the decided behavior.
Regenerate backend/openapi.json/frontend types if the response shape changes.

decisions.decision: An already-open position's displayed profit target (GET /api/portfolio/risk's new RiskPosition.profit_target field) is computed regardless of that ticker's current live signal -- NOT gated to a fresh BUY the way GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis's AnalysisResponse.profit_target still is. This explicitly revisits backend-profit-target's original decision, which applied the same BUY-only gate to both the fresh-signal analysis endpoint and (implicitly, since it didn't exist as a distinct field yet) any future open-position surface, reasoning entirely from the long-only stop-formula constraint (no symmetric short-side stop to pair with a SELL-side reward:risk ratio). That original rationale is still fully correct for a FRESH SELL signal (a candidate NEW short entry this app has no long-only-safe way to size a target for) -- it was never actually about HOLD, and doesn't apply at all to an ALREADY-OPEN long position: a held position in this app's portfolio model is unconditionally long regardless of what today's live signal for that ticker happens to read, so there's no short-side ambiguity to avoid computing a target for. Ch. 53, read directly (docs/ideas.md's own correction, added when researching this exact task): 'a target set at entry ... is meant to be tracked for the life of the trade, not recomputed only while the signal happens to say BUY' -- a held position already has a real entry to track, unlike a fresh-signal candidate that doesn't exist yet without a BUY. Implementation-wise, suggest_profit_target (app.portfolio.profit_target) was never given a signal parameter and never enforced any gate internally in the first place -- the BUY-only behavior on /analysis has always been that caller's own choice (get_analysis's own `if result.signal == 'BUY' else None`), so this task required zero domain-layer change: app/portfolio/profit_target.py's suggest_profit_target/ProfitTarget/_weekly_channel_bounds/_nearest_resistance_price are all byte-for-byte unchanged (confirmed via git diff -- only their docstrings were reworded to state explicitly that the function itself is signal-agnostic and that the two callers now deliberately differ). All the actual behavior change is in app/api/routers/portfolio.py's get_risk, which now calls suggest_profit_target (with a fresh app.signals.support_resistance.detect_support_resistance_zones pass over that position's own daily_ohlcv, plus its already-fetched weekly_ohlcv) for every position that reaches the per-position loop, with no signal check at all -- get_risk doesn't even compute a live signal for RiskPosition in the first place (unlike GET /api/portfolio's PositionOut.signal, from a separate _compute_position_signal helper), so there was no existing gate to remove, only a new unconditional call to add. Rejected alternatives: (a) keep the BUY-only gate for RiskPosition too, requiring get_risk to additionally call analyse()/_compute_position_signal per position just to check signal == 'BUY' before computing profit_target -- rejected as directly contradicting ch. 53's own text once read directly, and as inconsistent with this exact same endpoint's own pre-existing exit_flags, which the verify-elder-signal skill's own Portfolio Risk Overlay checklist already documents as required to be 'evaluated independently of the fresh-entry signal logic' (a HOLD signal must not suppress a stop-hit/6%-rule exit flag) -- profit_target for an open position is the same category of existing-position risk/reward context, not a fresh-entry decision, and should follow the identical independence principle; (b) literally freeze the target at whatever it would have been computed as on the position's own historical entry_date (fetching/slicing daily+weekly OHLCV back to entry_date and recomputing the channel/zones from only that historical window, rather than today's data) -- rejected as reading 'a target set at entry ... is tracked for the life of the trade' too literally: the phrase is contrasting 'tracked continuously' against 'gated by today's signal', not mandating a frozen historical snapshot: no other computation in this app (protective_stop, exit_flags, position_risk_pct) uses entry-date-only market data -- they're all computed off CURRENT price/history, and a profit target computed from stale months-old channel/zone data would be a materially different, larger feature (new OHLCV-as-of-a-past-date fetching/slicing this task's own checklist doesn't ask for) with no textual requirement in ch. 53 forcing that specific interpretation over the simpler 'don't gate on live signal, otherwise compute the same way' reading.
decisions.rationale: See the decision text above for the full reasoning against both rejected alternatives; kept in one entry since the 'what' and 'why' are inseparable for this exact judgment call.

decisions.decision: profit_target on RiskPosition degrades independently to null (a ValueError computing it, or neither target technique producing a candidate, sets profit_target=None for just that one position) rather than excluding the whole position from the positions list the way a protective_stop/exit_flags failure does.
decisions.rationale: Every other field on RiskPosition (protective_stop, position_risk_pct, exit_flags) is load-bearing for the 2%/6% rule math itself -- a position that can't produce one of those genuinely can't be risk-evaluated at all, so all-or-nothing exclusion (this endpoint's pre-existing, unchanged behavior) is correct for them. profit_target is purely supplementary informational context (same category as AnalysisResponse.profit_target on the /analysis endpoint, which is independently nullable there too) with zero downstream effect on total_open_risk_pct/six_percent_rule_breached/two_percent_rule_breached -- excluding an otherwise-fully-risk-evaluable position from the entire response just because its own support/resistance/channel pass happened to raise (e.g. a genuinely malformed daily frame missing 'volume', which detect_support_resistance_zones requires but protective_stop/evaluate_exit_flags don't) would silently hide real, correct 2%/6% rule risk data behind an unrelated failure. Verified this degrade path is actually reachable (not just theoretical) with a hand-built daily frame missing only 'volume' -- protective_stop/evaluate_exit_flags both succeed on it (they only need low/close), while detect_support_resistance_zones's own _validate_columns correctly raises ValueError -- and added an integration test asserting the position still appears with its other fields (including protective_stop) intact.

decisions.decision: The elder-signal-reviewer pass required by this task's checklist was done as scrutiny applied directly during implementation (per this task's own dispatch note that this is an accepted alternative to a separate agent pass), not as a separately dispatched agent run -- walked the verify-elder-signal skill's full 'Portfolio Risk Overlay' checklist against the diff: 2%/6% rule computation is untouched (still off current equity/position risk, never entry-time values); protective_stop's swing-low-minus-volatility-buffer formula is untouched; and the specific principle 'existing-position exit flags are evaluated independently of the fresh-entry signal logic -- a HOLD signal must not suppress a stop-hit or 6%-rule-breach exit flag' is the exact precedent this task's own change extends to profit_target (a second existing-position field now also independent of the fresh-entry signal, consistent with -- not in tension with -- that already-documented principle). No mismatch found between docs/Analyse.md and the implementation; docs/Analyse.md §7's 'Profit target' section and docs/architecture/API.md's GET /api/portfolio/risk section were both updated in this same change to describe the new two-callers-differ behavior, rather than leaving either stale.
decisions.rationale: Recorded explicitly per the verify-elder-signal skill's own 'Before calling a divergence deliberate, check the corresponding task's decisions array' guidance and CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule -- this checklist item's completion criteria (what was checked, against what, with what result) needs to be independently verifiable by a later reader, not just a checked box.

decisions.decision: Fixed PR #224 review blocking finding 1 (stop-value inconsistency) by adding an optional `stop: float | None = None` parameter to `suggest_profit_target` (app.portfolio.profit_target): when given, that value is used verbatim for `distance_to_stop`/`reward_risk_ratio` instead of the function deriving its own via `stop_from_price_action(daily_ohlcv, ...)` on the full (today's-bar-included) frame. `get_risk` (app.api.routers.portfolio) now passes its own already-computed `stops[position.id]` (itself `protective_stop(position, daily_ohlcv.iloc[:-1])`, i.e. the exact value `RiskPosition.protective_stop` reports) into this new parameter, so `profit_target`'s internal reward:risk math can never again disagree with that same position's own `protective_stop` field within one API response. `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis` (get_analysis) is unaffected -- it has no separate `protective_stop` field to desync from, so it omits the new parameter and keeps deriving its own stop from the full `daily_ohlcv` exactly as before (verified via the existing, unmodified `TestNoCandidateOrEmptyInput`/`TestRewardRiskRatioFlagging`/etc. unit tests, which never pass `stop`, still passing unchanged). Added a new integration test (`TestProfitTarget.test_profit_target_never_disagrees_with_this_position_s_own_protective_stop`, tests/integration/test_portfolio_risk.py) that reproduces the reviewer's own discrepancy pattern (an anomalous today-bar low that pulls a full-frame swing-low stop far below the `iloc[:-1]` one), asserts the two stops genuinely differ for that fixture (so the test isn't vacuous), then asserts `profit_target`'s implied stop matches `protective_stop` exactly -- plus unit-level coverage in `TestExplicitStopOverride` (tests/unit/test_portfolio_profit_target.py) for the `stop` parameter itself (verbatim override, backward-compatible omission, and the `distance_to_stop <= 0` guard still applying to an explicit override). Rejected alternative: having `get_risk` call `suggest_profit_target` with the already-`iloc[:-1]`-sliced `daily_ohlcv` itself (so the function's own internal stop derivation would naturally match) instead of adding a `stop` parameter -- rejected because `suggest_profit_target` also uses `daily_ohlcv` to derive `current_price` (`daily_ohlcv["close"].iloc[-1]`), and slicing off today's bar there would silently desync `current_price` from `position.current_price`/the rest of `RiskPosition` (which all reflect today's actual close), trading one desync bug for a different one; passing the already-correct stop value directly is the narrower, more surgical fix.
decisions.rationale: See the decision text above -- keeps what/why together per this task's own established convention for judgment calls not fully pinned down by docs/Analyse.md.

decisions.decision: Fixed PR #224 review blocking finding 2 (frontend never consuming the new field) by wiring RiskPanel's Profit Target column to read `RiskPosition.profit_target` directly off the already-in-hand `GET /api/portfolio/risk` response, and REMOVING the old per-row `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis` fetch entirely (not kept alongside) -- `PositionProfitTargetCell` is now a purely presentational component taking a `profitTarget: RiskPosition['profit_target'] | null` prop (no `ticker`/`signal` props, no `useQuery`), and the now-unused `usePositionProfitTarget.ts` hook/query was deleted outright. Updated the two now-stale/false comments the review flagged: `PositionProfitTargetCell`'s own doc comment now explains what was removed and why (it previously fetched `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis` gated on `signal === 'BUY'`, which is exactly the BUY-only gate this whole task exists to remove for held positions), and `RiskPanel.tsx`'s column comment no longer claims `RiskPosition` has no `profit_target` field. Also updated `features/portfolio/components/metricHelpContent.ts`'s `profitTargetHelp.interpretValue` to drop its `signal` parameter and its two signal-gated null-cause messages ('not applicable, signal is currently HOLD/SELL' and 'signal couldn't be computed') -- both were specifically about the BUY-only gate that no longer exists for this field; a null `RiskPosition.profit_target` now only ever means 'neither technique currently produces a candidate' (or the rarer column-validation degrade), the same single cause `suggest_profit_target`'s own domain-layer docstring documents. `features/stocks/components/metricHelpContent.ts`'s OWN separate `profitTargetHelp` (for `ProfitTargetDisplay`/`AnalysisResponse.profit_target` on the stock-detail page) is untouched -- that field remains genuinely BUY-only, so its signal-gated messaging is still accurate. Rejected alternative (explicitly considered per the review's own 'decide and record' prompt): keeping BOTH the new field-read AND the old per-row `/analysis` fetch (e.g. falling back to the fetch only when `RiskPosition.profit_target` is absent) -- rejected as pure redundant complexity with no behavioral upside: `GET /api/portfolio/risk` now computes `profit_target` unconditionally for every position that reaches its per-position loop (this same task's own backend decision above), so the two sources would never actually disagree or usefully complement each other, and the already-filed `frontend-profit-target-display-followups` non-blocking finding (this exact per-row-fetch's N+1/no-batching cost) is fully resolved as a side effect of removing the fetch outright, not just deferred.
decisions.rationale: See the decision text above -- the review explicitly asked this exact judgment call ('decide and record') rather than leaving it implicit.

decisions.decision: Fixed PR #224's second needs_work pass (stale/self-contradictory ProfitTargetOut field descriptions in backend/app/api/schemas.py) by rewording price/distance_to_stop/distance_to_target's descriptions to be caller-agnostic -- describing the price/stop/target in terms of 'current close' and 'right now' generically, and explicitly noting that the fresh-BUY-vs-open-position distinction is scoped by the parent field (AnalysisResponse.profit_target vs RiskPosition.profit_target), not baked into this shared nested schema -- rather than assuming one specific caller the way the prior wording ('for this fresh BUY signal', 'if entered at today's close') did. Both parent fields' own descriptions already correctly stated their respective BUY-only/signal-agnostic scoping before this fix; only ProfitTargetOut's own three field descriptions needed to stop contradicting whichever parent pointed at them. Regenerated backend/openapi.json (python scripts/export_openapi.py) and frontend/src/api/types.ts (npm run generate:api-types) -- diff confined to exactly these three description strings, verified via git diff. Also re-ran scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py (clean -- this fix doesn't touch the weekly-channel wording it guards), the full backend pytest suite (1109 passed), ruff/mypy on the changed file (clean), and frontend tsc --noEmit (clean, confirming types.ts's regenerated description strings didn't break any consumer).
decisions.rationale: Recorded per this task's own established convention of keeping what/why together for each review-driven fix, and per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule that a fix this specific (exact reworded text, exact regeneration commands run) needs to be independently verifiable by a later reader rather than only visible in the diff itself.

comments.summary: (Prior needs_work pass, now fixed) BLOCKING (stale/self-contradictory OpenAPI schema documentation): ProfitTargetOut's price/distance_to_stop/distance_to_target descriptions assumed a fresh-BUY-only, entered-today trade, contradicting RiskPosition.profit_target's own signal-agnostic description that points at the same shared schema. FIXED in commit 9ac62df6: reworded all three to be caller-agnostic ('at its current close' / 'right now', explicitly noting the BUY-only-vs-signal-agnostic distinction is scoped by the parent field, not this shared nested schema). Re-review, independently verified rather than just re-read: (1) read the reworded text against docs/Analyse.md §7 and against both parent fields' own descriptions (AnalysisResponse.profit_target, still correctly BUY-only; RiskPosition.profit_target, still correctly signal-agnostic) -- confirmed accurate for both callers without losing the concrete formula-level content (ch. 53/58 references, SafeZone/stop_from_price_action/protective_stop mentions all retained); (2) diffed backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts against a from-scratch regeneration (`python scripts/export_openapi.py`) -- zero diff, confirming the committed snapshot matches and the change really is confined to the three description strings (no accidental schema/type change); (3) ran a fresh, independent grep sweep across backend/app, frontend/src, docs/architecture, and docs/Analyse.md for 'fresh BUY'/'today's close'/'entered at today's close' wording that might still incorrectly describe RiskPosition.profit_target specifically -- every remaining hit correctly scopes to AnalysisResponse's own still-BUY-only field, `_determine_signal`'s own unrelated BUY-gating, or module/function docstrings already reworded in prior rounds to be caller-agnostic; the one non-blocking exception found is filed below.

Non-blocking (stale doc comment, same class of finding this task's prior two review rounds each caught in one more place): docs/architecture/Backend.md's file-tree listing still describes `profit_target.py` as 'suggested profit target + reward:risk ratio for a fresh BUY (Analyse.md §7)' -- true of its original caller but no longer true of the module as a whole now that `GET /api/portfolio/risk` also calls it unconditionally for every open position regardless of signal. Not blocking: it's a one-line file-tree inline comment in the architecture doc (not the OpenAPI contract, not a field-level description, and doesn't create a self-contradiction within one API response the way the now-fixed ProfitTargetOut issue did), and every other place this same distinction matters (the module's own docstring, docs/Analyse.md §7, docs/architecture/API.md's endpoint sections) was correctly updated to describe the two-callers-differ behavior. Filed as a checklist entry on backend-profit-target-open-position-followups rather than left only in this comment.

Non-blocking, pre-existing (not introduced by this PR -- traced via `git show main:...` to confirm it predates this task, landing with PR #222/backend-profit-target-weekly-channel): ProfitTargetOut.distance_to_target's schema description states 'Always > 0 by construction (both target techniques only ever produce a price above current close)', but `suggest_profit_target`'s own domain-layer docstring (backend/app/portfolio/profit_target.py, also pre-existing, untouched by this PR) explicitly documents a real degenerate case where the channel-derived target equals current price exactly (distance_to_target == 0) when the weekly Autoenvelope's rolling average deviation is exactly 0 across the whole lookback window -- an overstated invariant in the OpenAPI-exposed field description. Independently confirmed via `code-review` (background pass) and traced myself with `git diff main...HEAD`/`git show main:...` on both files to confirm this specific text is untouched by this task's diff and unrelated to the BUY-only-vs-signal-agnostic distinction this task's own checklist is about -- not blocking this PR (a different, already-merged task introduced it, and it doesn't relate to what this task changed), but a real, fixable inaccuracy worth tracking. Filed on the followups task rather than left only here.

BLOCKING (stale/self-contradictory OpenAPI schema documentation): ProfitTargetOut's own field-level descriptions (backend/app/api/schemas.py) still describe a fresh-BUY-only, entered-today trade -- price: 'Suggested profit target price for this fresh BUY signal'; distance_to_stop: 'if entered at today's close'; distance_to_target: 'if entered at today's close'. This same ProfitTargetOut schema is now also used verbatim for RiskPosition.profit_target (backend/app/api/schemas.py:429, added by this PR's own first commit), which is explicitly NOT BUY-gated and represents an ALREADY-open position with a real past entry, not a hypothetical fresh entry today. The committed backend/openapi.json (the single source of truth the frontend builds against per CLAUDE.md) now ships a self-contradiction within one response: RiskPosition.profit_target's own field description correctly says 'computed regardless of that ticker's current live signal being BUY', while every field on the ProfitTargetOut object it points to still asserts the opposite framing. This is the same class of gap the prior needs_work pass blocked on (stale/false text left unfixed elsewhere while other files were carefully updated) -- this task's decisions/docstrings/docs/Analyse.md/docs/architecture/API.md were all updated to describe the two-callers-differ behavior, but ProfitTargetOut's own three field descriptions were missed. Fix: reword price/distance_to_stop/distance_to_target's descriptions to be caller-agnostic (e.g. 'at the position's current price' or 'relative to current price', not 'today's close'/'fresh BUY signal'), matching how RiskPosition.profit_target's and AnalysisResponse.profit_target's own descriptions already correctly scope the BUY-only/not-BUY-only distinction at the field level that actually differs, rather than baking a caller-specific assumption into the shared nested schema.

Considered and rejected as a false positive (raised by this review's own code-review pass, verified and found not to hold): app.portfolio.risk.stop_from_price_action's docstring says it was factored out for a caller with no Position to hand it '(e.g. app.portfolio.profit_target.suggest_profit_target, computing a stop-distance for a ticker's fresh BUY signal rather than an already-held position)'. Traced whether this is now false given get_risk calls suggest_profit_target for every open position: it is NOT false -- get_risk always passes its own already-computed stop into suggest_profit_target's new stop parameter (this same PR's fix for the other blocking finding), so suggest_profit_target's internal stop_from_price_action(daily_ohlcv, ...) call (profit_target.py:292) only ever actually executes when stop is None, which today is exclusively the AnalysisResponse/fresh-BUY caller. The docstring's specific claim remains accurate for every path that actually reaches it. No action needed.

(Prior needs_work pass, now fixed) BLOCKING (correctness): get_risk's new profit_target computation uses a different protective stop than the very same RiskPosition's own protective_stop field, so the two can disagree within one API response. stops[position.id] (RiskPosition.protective_stop, and the stop position_risk_pct/evaluate_exit_flags use) is deliberately computed from daily_ohlcv.iloc[:-1] (excluding today's bar) -- get_risk's own docstring explains this exact choice exists to avoid a lookahead desync between today's close and today's stop. But the new `suggest_profit_target(daily_by_id[e.position.id], ..., weekly_ohlcv=...)` call passes the FULL daily_by_id[id] frame (today's bar included), and suggest_profit_target internally calls stop_from_price_action on that full frame to derive distance_to_stop/reward_risk_ratio/meets_minimum_reward_risk -- a different stop value than protective_stop reports for that same position. Independently verified this is a real, not just theoretical, discrepancy: for a fixture where the latest bar's low is a new extreme, stop_from_price_action(full_frame) = 106.04 vs stop_from_price_action(frame.iloc[:-1]) = 127.30 -- a ~21-point difference on the same underlying data. FIXED in commit 55b2b9d: suggest_profit_target now takes an optional `stop` parameter used verbatim when given; get_risk passes its already-computed `stops[e.position.id]` into it. Re-review: traced the actual variable reuse (`stop = stops[e.position.id]` at portfolio.py:718, passed unchanged to both `protective_stop=stop` and `suggest_profit_target(stop=stop)`); temporarily reverted the fix and confirmed the new integration test (TestProfitTarget.test_profit_target_never_disagrees_with_this_position_s_own_protective_stop) genuinely fails without it (implied_stop=-13.72 vs expected 127.3), then restored it and confirmed the test passes -- the reproduction is real, not vacuous.

(Prior needs_work pass, now fixed) BLOCKING (task purpose unmet + stale/false comments shipped): the frontend never read the new RiskPosition.profit_target field -- RiskPanel's Profit Target column still fetched GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis per row, gated on signal === 'BUY', so a held position whose signal had drifted to HOLD/SELL still showed an em dash, and two now-false comments shipped claiming RiskPosition carries no profit_target. FIXED in commit 55b2b9d: RiskPanel.tsx now passes `profitTarget={row.profit_target ?? null}` directly; PositionProfitTargetCell is now purely presentational (no ticker/signal props, no useQuery); usePositionProfitTarget.ts hook deleted entirely (decided against keeping both fetch paths, per the review's own 'decide and record' prompt -- see this task's decisions). Re-review: grepped for remaining usePositionProfitTarget references (none, only a historical doc-comment mention of what was removed); ran RiskPanel.test.tsx's new coverage directly, confirming a BUY row (AAPL, $245.00/2.0:1) and a HOLD row (MSFT, $420.00/0.8:1) both render distinct real profit targets -- the exact drifted-signal symptom this task exists to fix is genuinely gone.

Non-blocking (efficiency): GET /api/portfolio/risk now runs a full whole-history support/resistance detection pass (detect_support_resistance_zones) plus a second full weekly-Autoenvelope + swing-low pass (inside suggest_profit_target) for every position on every request, uncached -- none of which existed on this endpoint before. If this endpoint is polled (RiskPanel's usage suggests it is), this multiplies per-poll CPU cost by N extra heavy, previously-nonexistent passes with no memoization, unlike the already-computed stops/daily_by_id/weekly_by_id this same loop deliberately caches for reuse within one request. Not blocking on its own (correctness is fine, and today's data sizes make this cheap in practice), but worth tracking given the trend of this endpoint accumulating uncached whole-history passes. Still tracked (unchanged) on backend-profit-target-open-position-followups; no new non-blocking findings from this re-review pass.
